profile.address: 1513, North Arendell Avenue, Zebulon, Wake County, North Carolina, 27597
profile.reading:
This building at 1513 North Arendell Avenue in Zebulon, a small town in eastern Wake County roughly twenty five miles from downtown Raleigh, is identified in property and mapping records as a BB&T data center, a name it carries from Branch Banking and Trust Company, the North Carolina bank that operated it before a 2019 merger changed the company's name and ownership structure.

BB&T traced its history to 1872, when it was founded in Wilson, North Carolina, and it grew over the following century and a half into one of the largest regional banks in the southeastern United States, eventually headquartered in Winston Salem. In December 2019, BB&T combined with SunTrust Banks of Atlanta in a merger of equals that created Truist Financial Corporation, headquartered in Charlotte, which by combined assets became one of the ten largest commercial banks in the country. As with most large bank mergers, the combined company inherited both predecessor banks' back office and technology real estate rather than immediately consolidating every facility, and buildings such as this one in Zebulon appear to have continued operating under their legacy name in public records even as the parent company's brand and reporting structure changed.

Wake County and the broader Raleigh Durham region grew rapidly as a corporate and technology hub in the 2000s and 2010s, and banks in particular built out back office, operations, and data processing capacity in suburban and exurban parts of the county where land and power were more available than downtown, a pattern this Zebulon site fits. Truist has not published square footage, power capacity, tier rating, or a construction date for this specific building, and no announcement, permit filing, or trade press coverage describing it as a named project could be found. That silence is itself typical of how large regional banks handle single tenant, mission critical technology buildings. Unlike a colocation provider marketing available capacity to prospective tenants, a bank's own data processing facility exists purely to support internal operations such as core banking systems, transaction processing, and disaster recovery, and the institution has no commercial reason to publish the kind of specifications a customer facing operator would.

reading.body:
No megawatt capacity is published for this facility. Truist Financial's own site and Wikipedia contain no address, square footage, or power specification for the BB&T Data Center in Zebulon, Wake County. Without published IT load, the number of racks or accelerators this campus can host cannot be estimated.

The facility is mapped in OpenStreetMap at 1513 North Arendell Avenue, Zebulon, but sits outside the published capacity ranking in North Carolina. Five of the state's 19 mapped data center facilities publish power figures totaling 50.3 MW. This campus contributes nothing to that total.

For a reader assessing whether this campus matters to AI scaling, the absence of published specifications is disqualifying. Compute density, power availability, and grid position cannot be read from operator disclosures. The facility exists in the real estate record but remains opaque to capacity planning.
